question: A 67-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 4-month history of fatigue and weight loss. Physical examination shows jaundice. The liver is palpated 3 cm below the right costal margin. Serum studies show an elevated alpha-fetoprotein and a prolonged prothrombin time. Genetic analysis of a liver biopsy specimen shows a G:C to T:A transversion in codon 249 of the gene coding for the TP53 protein in affected cells. Which of the following risk factors is most specific to the patient's condition?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Jaundice" -> "Liver palpated 3 cm below right costal margin" -> "Elevated alpha-fetoprotein" -> "Prolonged prothrombin time" -> "G:C to T:A transversion in codon 249 of TP53 gene" -> "Liver cancer" -> "Dietary aflatoxin exposure" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Jaundice" -> "Liver palpated 3 cm below right costal margin" -> "Elevated alpha-fetoprotein" -> "Prolonged prothrombin time" -> "G:C to T:A transversion in codon 249 of TP53 gene" -> "Liver cancer" -> "Specific risk factor: Dietary aflatoxin exposure" -> 90%
analysis: The patient's presentation with jaundice, elevated alpha-fetoprotein, prolonged prothrombin time, and a specific genetic mutation in the TP53 gene (codon 249) associated with hepatocellular carcinoma points towards a diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma. Among the given options, dietary aflatoxin exposure is the most specific risk factor for hepatocellular carcinoma development in this patient.
